flagged.evidence: The Statement requires parity and |p(x)|≤1 but omits deg p≤d. The cited completion theorem requires degree at most d, and the phase-sequence lemma gives deg PΦ≤d. For d=0, p(x)=x² meets the written conditions but cannot be the real part of a degree-zero PΦ.

The proof says the rational search “terminates because a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots.” Its cited real-field and ordered-field dependencies do not establish that the enumerated rationals in (-1,1) form an infinite candidate set. Finiteness of the root set alone does not license termination; an elementary observation such as the infinitely many distinct rationals 1/n in the interval closes this small gap.
